answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by granting capability tokens only against verified, externally anchored receipts: each identity must present a signed proof of real work done for an independent service, like a comet leaving a checkable trail. A quorum of established peers validates each receipt, and one real-world credential can anchor only one identity. The old fable of a thousand free accounts fails because every fake needs a fresh receipt plus a quorum fee; a plume of overlapping proofs exposes the fraud, so an attacker pays a real-world price per Sybil while an honest agent pays once.
